process_area.title: Facilities Management Strategy, IFM Provider & SLA Governance

value_stream.name: Integrated Facilities Management, Workplace Services & Building Automation

fields.Owner: Head of Facilities / Store Operations Support
fields.Participants: COO, Store Ops (VS-07), Real Estate (VS-97/VS-20), Procurement (VS-34), Finance (VS-17.4)
fields.Trigger: Strategy refresh; growth (10–15 stores/yr); cost/service pressure
fields.Volume: Enterprise footprint (~205 sites; ~1.6–3.0M sqm selling + ~130,000 sqm DC + ~3,000 sqm HQ)

Controls: - CTL-644 (ensure controlled execution — Facilities Management Strategy, IFM Provider & SLA Governance (PA-138.1).)
- CTL-644: IFM operating model approved by COO; strategy aligned to corporate plan (VS-33)
Cross-references: - links to VS-97/VS-20 (real estate), VS-07 (store ops), VS-34 (procurement), VS-33 (strategy), VS-37 (growth), VS-134 (OCM)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fragmentation risk**: Each site/service contracted separately → overlap, gaps, leakage; mitigated by integrated IFM operating model
- **Provincial-capacity risk**: Uneven local contractor quality outside metro hubs; mitigated by cluster/national provider strategy
System Touchpoints: - IFM/CAFM platform strategy; real estate portfolio (VS-97/VS-20); store ops (VS-07); procurement (VS-34); strategy (VS-33)

steps.activity: Facilities define the IFM operating model — in-house vs outsourced per service line (cleaning, pest, guarding, HVAC, grounds), single-source IFM vs best-of-breed, and the site-cluster structure across the archipelago
Facilities set the facilities strategy and standards (service levels, response times, sustainability, safety, customer-experience impact), aligned to corporate strategy (VS-33) and growth (VS-37)
Facilities document the model, obtain executive approval, sequence rollout with OCM (VS-134), and resource the facilities org

fields.Trigger: Contract renewal; new service line; new-store cluster

workflows.name: IFM Provider Strategy, Sourcing & Contract Management

Controls: - CTL-644 (ensure controlled execution — Facilities Management Strategy, IFM Provider & SLA Governance (PA-138.1).)
- CTL-644: facilities contracts with SLA/penalty/exit clauses; ABC due diligence (VS-86.3); insurance verified
Cross-references: - links to VS-34 (procurement), VS-34.2 (service-provider mgmt), VS-100.3 (legal/contracts), VS-98 (contingent workforce), VS-86.3 (ABC)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lock-in risk**: Long contract with underperforming provider; mitigated by performance clauses and exit terms
- **ABC risk**: Facilities contracts (cash-rich, relationship-based) carry bribery exposure; mitigated by ABC controls (VS-86.3) and due diligence
System Touchpoints: - Contract repository (VS-34.2/VS-100.3); procurement (VS-34); contingent workforce (VS-98); risk (VS-21.2)

steps.activity: Facilities/Procurement run RFP/sourcing for IFM service lines (cleaning, pest, guarding, HVAC, grounds, cafeteria), evaluating capability, coverage, price, safety/ESG, and references

Facilities/Procurement/Legal structure contracts (SLA, scope, pricing, performance penalties, termination, insurance, ABC compliance links to VS-86.3), and onboard the provider (links to VS-98 contingent workforce)
Facilities manage the contract lifecycle (renewal, scope change, performance), and consolidate providers for leverage where sensible

fields.Participants: Store Ops (VS-07), DC Ops (VS-04), HQ Admin, Providers
fields.Trigger: Operating-model setup; service review; site-type change
fields.Volume: Service catalog across ~205 sites × service lines

Automation Opportunity: - Service-catalog templating per site type; SLA-differentiation rules
Controls: - CTL-644 (ensure controlled execution — Facilities Management Strategy, IFM Provider & SLA Governance (PA-138.1).)
- CTL-644: service catalog boundary vs equipment maintenance (VS-20.3) documented; SLAs in contracts
Cross-references: - links to VS-20.3 (equipment maintenance — boundary), VS-07 (store ops), VS-04 (DC ops), VS-73 (waste), VS-23.2 (security)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Undefined-scope risk**: Overlap/gap between equipment maintenance (VS-20.3) and building services; mitigated by clear catalog boundaries
- **One-size risk**: Same SLA for a 24/7 store and an office; mitigated by criticality-differentiated SLAs
System Touchpoints: - CAFM/IFM service catalog; provider contracts (W4170); store ops comms (VS-07 W1775)

steps.activity: Facilities define the service catalog — hard services (HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire systems, elevators, BMS) and soft services (cleaning, pest, guarding, grounds, waste, cafeteria, mailroom) — per site type (store/DC/HQ)
Facilities set SLAs per service (frequency, response/resolution times, quality standards) differentiated by site criticality (24/7 store vs DC vs HQ) and codify in provider contracts (W4170)
Facilities publish the catalog/SLA to sites and providers, train site staff on how to request/report, and govern SLA changes

fields.Owner: Facilities Asset Manager / Real Estate (VS-97/VS-20) / Fixed Assets (VS-35)
fields.Participants: Real Estate (VS-97/VS-20), Engineering (VS-20.2), Capex (VS-40), DC Ops (VS-04)
fields.Trigger: Site acquisition/opening (VS-37); condition survey; capex trigger
fields.Volume: ~205 buildings × fabric/systems (roof, structure, HVAC, fire, electrical, plumbing, elevators)

workflows.name: Facilities Asset Register & Building Condition Management

Automation Opportunity: - Condition-survey mobile capture; capex-trigger auto-flag from condition rating
Controls: - CTL-644 (ensure controlled execution — Facilities Management Strategy, IFM Provider & SLA Governance (PA-138.1).)
- CTL-644: register boundaries vs VS-35/VS-20.3/VS-97 documented; landlord-tenant responsibility mapped (VS-42)
Cross-references: - links to VS-97 (real estate), VS-35 (fixed assets), VS-20.3 (equipment — boundary), VS-40 (capex), VS-109 (remodel), VS-42/VS-97.2 (lease responsibility)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Boundary-confusion risk**: Building fabric vs FF&E/equipment vs real-estate asset — duplicate or missing; mitigated by clear register boundaries
- **Landlord-tenant risk**: Repair cost misallocated between BuildRight (tenant) and Property Mgmt (landlord); mitigated by lease-responsibility mapping (VS-42/VS-97.2)
System Touchpoints: - CAFM asset register; real-estate portfolio (VS-97); fixed assets (VS-35); capex (VS-40); remodel (VS-109); lease admin (VS-42/VS-97.2)
Time Estimate: - Annual survey ~0.5 FTE; ongoing register maintenance

steps.activity: Facilities maintain the building/fabric asset register (building systems, age, condition, warranty, replacement cost) distinct from FF&E/equipment (VS-35/VS-20.3), integrated with the real-estate portfolio (VS-97)

Facilities/Engineering conduct periodic building-condition surveys (roof, structure, HVAC, fire/life-safety, elevators, facade), rate condition, and identify capex/refurbishment triggers (links to VS-109 remodel, VS-40 capex)
Facilities feed condition data into capex planning (VS-40) and the remodel/refurbishment program (VS-109), and track landlord-vs-tenant repair responsibility (links to VS-42 lease admin, VS-97.2)
steps.r: Facilities Asset Mgr / Capex / Real Estate

fields.Participants: Providers/contractors, Store Ops (VS-07), DC Ops (VS-04), HSE (VS-24), Calibration (VS-115)
fields.Trigger: PM schedule cycle; OEM interval; compliance requirement
fields.Volume: ~205 sites × building systems (HVAC filters/coils, fire-system tests, elevator certs, generator, BMS calibration)

Automation Opportunity: - Auto PM scheduling from OEM intervals; completion/compliance auto-tracking; certificate-expiry alerts
Controls: - CTL-644 (ensure controlled execution — Facilities Management Strategy, IFM Provider & SLA Governance (PA-138.1).)
- CTL-644: PM completion tracked; statutory systems (fire/elevator/generator) cert-current (VS-24/VS-22)
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-22 (permits/fire), VS-115 (calibration), VS-40 (capex), W4174 (work-orders), VS-20.3 (equipment PM)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Compliance-gap risk**: Missed fire-system/elevator/generator cert → regulatory/safety exposure; mitigated by scheduled PM with completion tracking
- **Reactive-creep risk**: Deferred PM → more breakdowns; mitigated by PM-vs-reactive ratio monitoring (W4192)
System Touchpoints: - CAFM PM scheduling; work-order system (W4174); HSE (VS-24); calibration (VS-115); condition/capex (W4172/VS-40)

steps.activity: Facilities build the preventive-maintenance (PM) schedule per asset/system from OEM intervals, warranty, and compliance (fire-system, elevator, generator), and resource it across providers/sites
Facilities execute PM (HVAC service, fire-system test, elevator annual cert, generator load-test, BMS check), documenting completion and findings in the work-order system (W4174)
Facilities feed PM findings into condition/capex (W4172), coordinate with calibration where relevant (VS-115), and monitor PM-vs-reactive ratio (W4192)

fields.Participants: Site staff (VS-07/VS-04), Providers, HSE (VS-24), Store Ops
fields.Trigger: Site-reported issue (broken AC, leak, light out, pest sighting); emergency

Automation Opportunity: - Mobile work-order logging; auto-dispatch by service line/location; SLA-breach auto-escalation; photo/iot evidence
Controls: - CTL-644 (ensure controlled execution — Facilities Management Strategy, IFM Provider & SLA Governance (PA-138.1).)
- CTL-644: SLA adherence tracked; emergency path to VS-24.2/VS-69; completion verified with site
Cross-references: - links to VS-07 (store staff), VS-24.2 (emergency response), VS-69 (typhoon/disaster), VS-23.2 (security incidents), W4171 (SLA), W4178 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Response-breach risk**: Slow resolution closes a store/aisle; mitigated by SLA + escalation
- **Recurring-issue risk**: Same fault repeatedly logged → root cause unaddressed; mitigated by recurring-issue analytics (W4192)
System Touchpoints: - CAFM helpdesk/work-order system; provider dispatch; emergency response (VS-24.2/VS-69); SLA framework (W4171)
Time Estimate: - ~5 min log + dispatch; resolution per SLA; helpdesk tier-1 staffed by the IFM provider (VS-138.2) with ~1–2 in-house FTE for escalation and vendor management (within the 8-person Facilities & Real Estate team, profile §3.3)

steps.activity: Site staff log the issue via the facilities helpdesk (channel: app/phone/portal), triaged by criticality (safety/operations-impacting vs routine) and service line (W4171)
Facilities dispatch to the right provider/technician, track to SLA resolution (W4171), and escalate on breach; emergencies (fire/flood/power) trigger emergency response (VS-24.2/VS-69)
Facilities verify completion/quality with the site, close the work-order, capture cost, and analyze recurring issues (W4192)

fields.Participants: Compliance (VS-22), HSE (VS-24), LGU Affairs (VS-76), Engineering (VS-20.2), Insurance (VS-26.3)
fields.Trigger: Permit cycle; inspection; fire/life-safety test; regulatory change
fields.Volume: ~205 sites × permits/certs (BFP Fire Safety, elevator, electrical, sanitary, LGU building/occupancy)

Automation Opportunity: - Permit-expiry auto-alerts; inspection-finding auto-tracking; certificate repository
Controls: - CTL-644: permit/cert calendar with expiry tracking; fire/life-safety tests documented (VS-24); records retained (VS-88)
Cross-references: - links to VS-22.1 (permits), VS-76.1 (LGU), VS-24 (HSE/fire-life-safety), VS-88 (records), VS-26.3 (insurance), VS-21 (audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lapsed-permit risk**: Expired fire/elevator/occupancy cert → fines, closure, insurance invalidation; mitigated by expiry calendar + remediation
- **Inspection-fail risk**: Non-compliant fire/life-safety; mitigated by periodic testing and pre-inspection self-audit
System Touchpoints: - CAFM permit/cert calendar; permits (VS-22.1); LGU compliance (VS-76.1); HSE (VS-24); records (VS-88); insurance (VS-26.3)
Time Estimate: - Continuous compliance ~0.5–1 FTE; testing per cycle

steps.activity: Facilities/Compliance maintain the facilities-permit/certification calendar per site (BFP Fire Safety Inspection Certificate, elevator/escalator permits, electrical, sanitary, LGU occupancy/annual — links to VS-22.1, VS-76.1) and track expiry
Facilities/Engineering coordinate fire/life-safety testing (fire alarm, sprinkler, extinguisher, emergency lighting, exit routes) with HSE (VS-24.1/VS-24.2), and ensure BFP/code compliance
Facilities/Compliance manage regulator inspections (BFP, LGU, DENR), remediate findings, retain records (VS-88), and support insurance/audit (VS-26.3/VS-21)

fields.Trigger: Budget cycle; monthly review; vendor scorecard
fields.Volume: Facilities opex across ~205 sites (hard+soft services + utilities + maintenance)

workflows.name: Facilities Budget, Cost-to-Serve & Vendor Performance Governance

Automation Opportunity: - Spend/budget dashboards; provider-scorecard automation; cost-to-serve benchmarking
Controls: - CTL-644: facilities budget vs actual monitored; provider scorecards with consequences; cost-to-serve benchmarked
Cross-references: - links to VS-17.4 (finance), VS-34.3 (expense), VS-34 (procurement), VS-40 (capex), VS-133 (OpEx), W4178 (analytics), VS-135 (TBM)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Leakage risk**: Fragmented/overlapping service contracts overspend; mitigated by consolidated IFM and cost-to-serve visibility
- **Scorecard-inaction risk**: Poor providers retained; mitigated by consequence management
System Touchpoints: - Finance/budget (VS-17.4); expense monitoring (VS-34.3); provider scorecards (W4170); OpEx (VS-133); analytics (W4192)

steps.activity: Facilities/Finance build the facilities budget (per site/service line, utilities, maintenance, capex links to VS-40) with cost-to-serve baselines and benchmarks (PHP/sqm)
Facilities/Procurement measure provider performance (SLA adherence W4171, quality, cost, safety) via scorecards, manage consequences, and consolidate for leverage
Facilities/Finance monitor spend vs budget, identify leakage/overruns, report facilities cost-to-serve KPIs (W4192), and feed into OpEx (VS-133) and TBM where IT-facilities overlap
